stem: In which year was the voting age lowered from 21 to 18?
explanation: The voting age of 18 was set in 1969. Women won the vote on equal terms with men in 1928.
source: Handbook ch. 5 · British democracy and the government

stem: At the start of the 19th century, every adult man in Britain had the right to vote.
explanation: Only men over 21 who owned a certain amount of property could vote. The right to vote was widened gradually.
source: Handbook ch. 5 · British democracy and the government

stem: Why is the British constitution often described as unwritten?
options: It has never been approved by Parliament
It is not set out in one single document
It is kept secret from the public
It can only be changed by the monarch
explanation: The constitution is made up of laws, conventions and institutions rather than one written document.
source: Handbook ch. 5 · British democracy and the government

stem: What is the main role of civil servants?
options: To stand for election to Parliament
To judge cases in the criminal courts
To run election campaigns for parties
explanation: Civil servants help develop and carry out government policy and deliver public services.
source: Handbook ch. 5 · Devolution; The UK and the world

options: By central government and local taxes
explanation: Councils receive money from central government and raise local taxes, such as council tax.
source: Handbook ch. 5 · Devolution; The UK and the world

stem: Which kind of law is used to settle disputes between people or organisations?
explanation: Civil law settles disputes between individuals or groups. Criminal law deals with crimes punished by the courts.

stem: Which of these are criminal offences? Select TWO.
options: Disagreeing with a landlord about repairs
explanation: Selling tobacco to under-18s and carrying any weapon, even for self-defence, are crimes. Debts and landlord disputes are civil matters.

stem: It is against the law to smoke in nearly every enclosed public place in the UK.
explanation: Smoking tobacco is banned in nearly all enclosed public places, and signs show where you cannot smoke.

stem: Voting in local and national elections is one of the shared responsibilities of people in the UK.
explanation: Voting is listed among the shared responsibilities, although nobody can be forced to vote for a particular candidate.
source: Handbook ch. 5 · Your role in the community

stem: How are people chosen for jury service?
options: From people who pass a legal exam
At random from the electoral register
By applying to the local court
explanation: Jurors are picked at random from people on the electoral register.
source: Handbook ch. 5 · Your role in the community
